correctness.rationale:
At a predator-free endemic equilibrium, the infected-prey equation gives \(x=
u(\alpha+y)/ eta\). Substitution into the susceptible-prey equation produces an explicit quadratic. If \( eta K\le\alpha
u\), its factor form is strictly negative for every \(y>0\). If \( eta K>\alpha
u\), the quadratic has negative root product and therefore exactly one positive root. The symbolic verifier reconstructs this identity and checks exact examples.

evidence: Naji and Hasan (2012) give a unique endemic equilibrium in a different predator-absent SIS subsystem with mass-action infection and recovery.

Mortoja, Panja, and Mondal (2019), DOI 10.1016/j.egg.2018.100035, treat a related delayed Crowley--Martin disease-in-prey model, but the accessible abstract does not state the present quadratic or threshold.

originality.rationale: The primary paper prints a cubic, a three-positive-root sign case, and a sufficient condition lacking the carrying capacity \(K\). Searches of the exact title, DOI, parameter combination, and related eco-epidemiological equilibrium literature found no correction or equivalent source-specific classification. The closest older accessible full text concerns a different SIS/Crowley--Martin model and does not imply this saturated-incidence quadratic.
residual_risks: The full text of Mortoja, Panja, and Mondal (2019) was not available in the inspected lawful sources; it remains a plausible related-source risk.
A later unindexed author correction could exist despite the exact-title, DOI, author, and parameter searches.
The finding does not assess whether subsequent sections of the 2024 article ever use an alternative unpublished predator-free equilibrium calculation.

value.rationale: The correction collapses an advertised one-versus-three boundary-equilibrium multiplicity problem to a sharp zero-versus-one threshold, identifies the threshold as the disease-invasion condition at the prey-only state, and gives a concrete counterexample to the source's stated sufficient condition. This changes the boundary phase portrait rather than merely changing notation or a coefficient.
